NEW: Iran may be rebuilding nuclear weapons development capabilities at Minzadayi, northeast of Tehran, following Israeli strikes on March 3, 2026.
High resolution satellite imagery from September and October shows extensive cleanup, repairs, earthmoving operations and renewed vehicle activity at the compound.
The IDF previously identified the site as a covert facility developing key components for nuclear weapons.
Looks like Iran is attempting to restore its nuclear warhead research and development program again.
Inst for Science (@TheGoodISIS)
NEW Report: Significant Activity Identified at Minzadayi, an Iranian Nuclear Weapons Development Site
High resolution @vantortech satellite imagery from September and October 2026 shows significant renewed activity at Minzadayi, a nuclear weapons development compound northeast of Tehran revealed by Israel during the 2026 war.  The compound was attacked by Israel on March 3rd, 2026, destroying several buildings and likely underground structures. The recent satellite imagery indicates a return to regular vehicle activity around the site post extensive cleanup operation that included the clearing of rubble and debris and repair of damage on the hillside.  One area attacked in March 2026 shows ongoing earth moving activity.  The earth moving activity is occurring at a surface made to look like a courtyard where multiple craters could be seen following the attacks on the site in March 2026. Significant vehicle presence can be seen throughout the site between early September and early October 2026. Cars are parked outside the security perimeter in the parking lot, and many passenger vehicles and trucks can be seen inside the perimeter.  Given what is known about this compound, this activity may be indicative of an effort by Iran to reestablish a nuclear weapons development capability and to reconstitute what was lost in the attack on the compound.
Based on public reporting and statements released by the IDF, the nuclear weapons work carried out here likely involved research and development on nuclear warheads.  The IDF originally stated, that a “group of nuclear scientists operated covertly to develop a key component in the nuclear weapons system,” adding that “the complex is designed to enable the restoration of the required technology and the advancement of capabilities for the development of nuclear weapons.”
@IntelliTimes , released additional information on the compound.  In a post from September 24, 2026, it states that the nuclear weapons related infrastructure was established in 2022 and “absorbed part of the means from the nuclear warehouse,” a common reference to the Turquz Abad site revealed by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in September 2018.  Netanyahu revealed the site following Iran’s removal of more than a dozen shipping containers from the site that were assessed to hold nuclear material and equipment relevant to Iran’s nuclear weapons capabilities.[4]  When the IAEA visited Turquz Abad in March 2019, it found evidence that nuclear material or contaminated equipment had been present at the site and the IAEA Board has since been pressing Iran to answer the IAEA’s questions about the current whereabouts of said material and/or equipment. @IntelliTimes indicates Iran did not simply move the material and/or equipment to a new long term storage site but used the new site in northeast Tehran, aka Minzadayi, to establish an”  industrial nuclear headquarters for the reconstruction of research, development, and adaptation infrastructure for nuclear warheads,” including the means to “produce cores of enriched uranium and the explosive material required to cast into them the detonation chain.”[5]  The current renewed effort underway at this highly secure compound suggests that the work being conducted here is of top priority.
Read the report here: isis-online.org/isis-reports…
— http://nitter.meowing.monster/TheGoodISIS/status/2107526269462065613#m

🇺🇦 Some highlights from a recent Telegraph article on the Ukrainian operations on the Oleksandrivka front.
- The shaping operation enabling the armored maneuver elements of the operation took up to 8 months.
- Ukraine hacked the smartphones of Russian troops and used their social media (used in lieu of a proper BMS) messages to correct fires.
- Systemic targeting of UAS positions forced Russian UAS and C-UAS crews to fall back to safer positions further from the front.
- The mid-strike campaign focused on hitting logistical targets depleted frontline supplies in the area (seeing the same play out north of Lyman).
- Ukrainian infiltration teams went in first, avoiding Russian positions that were too fortified to take. Later recon units were tasked with clearing those positions.
- Ukrainian soldiers would cross rivers like the Vovcha by swimming across them and having fresh clothing and equipment delivered to them by drone afterwards.
- Once the ground had been cleared by the infantry, tanks rolled in to provide direct fire support against waves of Russian counterattacks.
